thread:
incident-bot: [PAGER] High 502/504 spike detected - api-gateway-eu (severity: P1)
incident-bot: error-rate: 35% over last 1m, latency p95: 2.8s, alert link: https://grafana/redwood/alerts/2471

dave-oncall: I'm taking pager. ack @incident-bot. oncall -> dave (eu-night).

ben: seeing a ton of upstream timeouts from edge -> app-proxy. `connect_timeout` spikes in the logs. starting grep now.

santiago: FYI we finished a canary rollout of cache-invalidator ~5m before the spike. not saying it's causal but flagging it. :eyes:

alice: Confirmed - /v1/generate route returning 502s and 504s. app-proxy logs show `upstream prematurely closed connection` across many hosts.

infra-bot: Runbook suggestion: enable regional fallback for EU to US until we stabilize. Command: `POST https://ops/api/routing/fallback -d '{"region":"eu","target":"us-west"}'` (requires ops-token)

ben: I ran the fallback (ops audit id: fa1b2c). Also scaled edge-pool-eu from 4 -> 8 nodes: `kubectl scale deploy/edge-pool-eu --replicas=8 -n infra`.

ciara: Customer impact: ~20% of EU traffic gets 502 currently. Several support tickets noting timeouts in the dashboard. Not yet classified as Major customer outage but trending.

maya: Can we temporarily increase upstream timeouts? nginx currently 30s - suggest 60s to give app-proxy more headroom while we investigate.

alice: rolling back cache-invalidator canary to prev stable now: `kubectl rollout undo deployment/cache-invalidator -n prod --to-revision=3`

ben: patching nginx config on app-proxy-*/pods: applying quick change. snippet:```
proxy_connect_timeout 60s;
proxy_read_timeout 60s;
proxy_send_timeout 60s;
```

alice: logs (excerpt):```
2026-11-03T12:43:21Z app-proxy-9f7 error "upstream prematurely closed connection" id=xyz host=cache-invalidator-2
2026-11-03T12:43:22Z app-proxy-3a1 timeout "read timeout" route=/v1/generate rt=31.2s
2026-11-03T12:43:23Z edge-4b2 error 502 upstream_connection_reset
```

dave-oncall: After scaling + fallback + timeout bump we see error-rate drop to ~8% in last 2m. Traces point to saturation on cache-invalidator pods - connection pool exhaustion.

santiago: I'm running a double-check on connection pool settings, also increasing max connections in the service mesh for cache-invalidator to see effect.

ciara: Support update drafted: "We experienced elevated 5xx errors in EU between 12:42-12:56 UTC. We mitigated via routing fallback to US and capacity scaling; some customers may have seen timeouts. We're continuing to monitor." :memo:

incident-bot: Follow-up reminder: create postmortem if duration > 30m OR customer-impact >= moderate. PD incident: https://pd/redwood/incidents/INC-2027

ben: handing off to night oncall @maya in 15m. Summary to include in ticket: rollback cache-invalidator canary, enabled eu->us-west fallback, scaled edge pool, bumped upstream timeouts, investigating connection pool limits.

maya: ack. I'll keep eyes overnight and follow up with a morning summary. please add any relevant logs to INC-2027.

dave-oncall: quick checklist for Maya:
- ensure fallback remains enabled until canary fully validated
- monitor errors/api-latency dashboard (p90/p95)
- if error-rate creeps >15% revert fallback and re-scale app-proxy pool
- gather flamegraphs/traces for cache-invalidator pods

ben: added notes + commands to INC-2027.also attaching audit ids and kubectl commands. :white_check_mark:

incident-bot: Scheduling readout meeting in #postmortems if postmortem required.

maya: thanks team — will post a short incident summary at start of shift and update when I see trend changes. Good handoff. :thumbsup:

dave-oncall: handing off -> maya at 2471000345. ending real-time triage. followups in INC-2027 and #postmortems.
